title: Bin El Ouidane reservoir, 26 Sep to 8 Oct 2026
summary: In the 12 days from 26 Sep to 8 Oct 2026 the lake barely changed, 29.82 km2 and then 29.91 km2, but the whole circle got brighter, with mean HH up 1.29 dB. The 8 Oct date carries two flags, so this sudden brightening should not be read as change on the ground.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: The lake changed by 0.09 km2, or 0.3%. HH turned brighter by more than 3 dB on 23.03 km2 and darker on only 0.17 km2. HV turned brighter on 8.01 km2, and mean HV rose by 0.79 dB.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: The brightening covers every type. Rough dry ground and fields had 11.74 km2 brighter in HH and rose 2.11 dB on average, and trees, shrub and rugged slopes had 5.66 km2 brighter. Built-up land, which should stay stable, rose 1.85 dB in HH, and the open water type rose 1.72 dB.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause: a processing offset in the 8 Oct product, since buildings brightened like fields within 12 days; reprocessed files would settle it. Possible cause: a wet surface after rain; local rain records for early October would check it.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: 8 Oct 2026 carries two flags: the lake water threshold moved more than 1.0 dB from the previous date, and backscatter over built-up land shifted more than 0.5 dB from its June-September median. Both lower confidence in every number from that date. Lake areas are approximate: 9.2% and 8.9% of the outline falls on land in the optical photo.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: Treat this pair as the clearest view of the October offset, not of land change. Check rain records for early October and ask NASA whether the October products will be reprocessed.
